title: Throughput envelope & conservative-surge autoscaler controller
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description:
Background:
We need an autoscaling controller for Dedicated pools that guarantees tenant throughput SLOs while preventing unsafe surge behavior that destabilizes the fleet. Recent incidents (see incident-2025-11-fleet-surge) showed uncontrolled scale-ups during short traffic spikes caused knock-on capacity exhaustion for colocated tenants.

Goal:
- Define a conservative 'throughput envelope' per pool and per-tenant that reconciles observed traffic, short-term forecasts, and a bounded surge budget.
- Implement a controller that chooses scaling actions by combining target metrics (tokens/s, request rate, p99 latency), short-term forecasts, and safety limits (surge budget, max-instances, cooling windows).
- Provide observable knobs for Platform and tenants, and a staged rollout plan with canary and soak tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller exposes target_metric choices: tokens_per_sec, rps, p99_latency.
- Scale-up is limited by surge_budget and per-pool max_instances; scale-down follows a conservative cooldown to avoid oscillation.
- On synthetic spike tests (see test-suite link), p95 latency remains within SLO and no more than 2x baseline instances are allocated by the controller during the spike window unless override is enabled.
- Dashboard panels show forecasted demand, headroom, pending_scale, and surge_consumed.

Design summary (high-level):
1) Metrics & targets:
   - Primary target: tokens_per_second (aggregated across pods for tenant/pool).
   - Secondary targets: requests_per_second (rps) and p99 generation latency.
   - Each target is evaluated on a fixed time window (default 30s for tokens/rps, 5m for latency).

2) Forecasting & smoothing:
   - Use an exponential weighted moving average (EWMA) for short-term smoothing and a 5-minute quantile forecasting model (95th) to capture bursts.
   - Forecast value F = max(EWMA_30s, quantile_5m_95).

3) Throughput envelope and headroom:
   - capacity = current_instances * instance_tokens_per_sec_profile (runtime telemetry).
   - required_capacity = max(F * safety_multiplier, observed_steady_plus_peak)
   - headroom = required_capacity - capacity (clamped to >= 0)
   - safety_multiplier defaults to 1.15 (15% headroom) but is configurable per-customer/pool.

4) Surge budget and safety limits:
   - surge_budget is a token budget that caps short-term burst additions. It is expressed as either: additional_instances_allowed or tokens/sec budget.
   - default_surge_instances = min(ceil(headroom / instance_tokens), 2) (hard cap 2 during canary).
   - global per-cluster cap: no more than 10% of spare GPUs consumed by surge at any time (platform-level knob).
   - cooldown_up = 30s evaluation window with immediate batch up to surge limit; cooldown_down = 10m conservative scale-down window to avoid thrash.

5) Scaling decision function (summary pseudocode):
   - Observe: observed_tps, ewma_30s, quantile_5m_95
   - Forecast F = max(ewma_30s, quantile_5m_95)
   - required_instances = ceil((F * safety_multiplier) / instance_tokens_per_sec)
   - surge_allowance = min(surge_budget_instances, max_surge_per_pool)
   - desired_instances = clamp(required_instances, min_instances, current_instances + surge_allowance, max_instances)
   - if desired_instances > current_instances: apply scale-up with rate_limiter(max_scale_up_per_minute)
   - if desired_instances < current_instances: require steady_decrease_condition (sustained below threshold for cooldown_down)

6) Rate limiting & governors:
   - max_scale_up_per_minute default = 1.5x of current_instances per minute but bounded by absolute instance count (configurable).
   - safety governor enforces: (a) do not consume > X% of cluster spare capacity, (b) respect tenant priority tiers (enterprise tenants may have higher surge budgets).

Trade-offs & rationale:
- Conservative defaults bias toward under-provisioning slightly to protect fleet stability; tenants can opt into aggressive surge mode with business justification.
- Keeping tokens/sec as primary target better aligns cost accounting and kernel-level performance profiles than pure RPS or latency signals.
- Longer scale-down cooldown reduces oscillation but increases short-term cost; default 10m chosen after replaying past traffic traces.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Controller core (go): implement decision loop, integrate with runtime telemetry API for instance_tokens_per_sec profile (ENG-XXXX).
- Forecast service: lightweight internal module (python) with EWMA + quantile aggregator; expose gRPC endpoint for controller to query 5m_95.
- Policy config: CRD-like per-pool JSON schema + API for tenants to set safety_multiplier, surge_budget, priority_tier.
- Observability: dashboards in Console; new metrics: scale_decision_reason, surge_consumed_tokens, forecast_window_value.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests: decision function edge cases, cooldown logic, governor limits.
- Integration: run controller in canary on dedicated-qa pool with synthetic spike harness (ref: /dashboards/throughput-tests).
- Stage rollout: canary (2 pools) -> gradual (20 pools) -> full; at each stage validate fleet spare capacity impact.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Throughput+Envelope+Design
- Spike test harness: https://internal.redwood.ai/drive/throughput-sim
- PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1245
- Incident notes: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2025-11-fleet-surge

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should tenant priority tiers be enforced as hard limits (preemptive) or soft hints (preferential surge allowance)? (PM/Infra decision)
- Precise global cluster cap (X% spare capacity for surge) -- currently proposing 10% but needs infra sign-off.
- KMS & audit impacts for Private deployments when controller autoscaling triggers provisioning (security review flagged).

Notes for assignee:
- Start implementation in controller core with simple forecast stub so we can run canary quickly.
- Coordinate with Observability (Rita) for dashboard panels and with Infra (Jamal) for cluster cap enforcement.

acceptance_criteria: Expose primary and secondary scaling targets (tokens_per_sec, rps, p99_latency) via policy schema.
Scale-ups respect surge_budget and do not exceed per-pool/max cluster caps.
Scale-down only after sustained under-utilization for cooldown_down (default 10m).
Dashboard shows scale decisions and surge consumption; alerts fire if >80% cluster surge cap used.
